customer_acme: Hey team — streaming stopped at ~80% of the response. I reconnected within ~6s and then got a full completion again. We appear to have been billed for two completions. Can you help?

maria_cs: sorry about that, can you paste the session_id and approximate timestamps?

customer_acme: session_id=srv-9f3b, initial start 2026-03-10T18:14:41Z, disconnect ~18:15:02Z, reconnect ~18:15:08Z. We send a Resume-Token and Idempotency-Key on reconnect.

maria_cs: thx — quick question: did the reconnect log return a 200 + resume_accept or a 202/new stream?

customer_acme: reconnect returned 200 but the stream included the remainder of the previous completion AND then another full completion after ~1s. So duplicated text. Billing shows two completion charges.

dan_engineer: (reading logs) I see a server-side line: `resume_attempt token=abc123 status=accepted offset=742` at 18:15:08. Then later `completion_finalized id=cmp-44a size=1892`. But there's also `resume_window_expired session=srv-9f3b elapsed=9.3s` around 18:15:17 which triggered fallback.

priya_sre: interesting — our resume window is 10s for that runtime. If the client acks the last chunk late or sends conflicting idempotency, we sometimes finalize the first generation then accept a fresh request. Could explain double finalize.

maria_cs: can you paste the reconnect headers they sent (customer said they included Idempotency-Key)?

customer_acme: here — ```
GET /stream/reconnect HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Resume-Token: abc123
Idempotency-Key: acme-req-20260310-18-15
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
```

dan_engineer: that Idempotency-Key looks fine. Two possible flows: 1) service accepted resume and continued (should not bill again), 2) resume window small variance + late ACK -> service finalized the prior run (billed) and then treated incoming reconnect as a new request, accepted it and produced new generation (billed). Logs you provided show both finalize and then new generation.

priya_sre: corroborating logs: `kv_cache_invalidate reason=late_ack session=srv-9f3b` then `new_request accepted id=cmp-55b`. So we recreated the output. I suspect the client sent the reconnect while server was in the process of finalizing the previous stream (race).

maria_cs: Sorry for the customer impact. Short term: we'll credit one completion. Longer term: infra follow-up to harden resume semantics when finalize and resume overlap.

dan_engineer: repro steps for infra: 1) start SSE streaming request with long generation. 2) simulate client disconnect at final token chunk but before server finalizes. 3) client reconnect after X ms with same Resume-Token and same Idempotency-Key. 4) observe double finalize when finalize latency > reconnect latency. Example script: ```bash
# simulate reconnect race
python repro/reconnect_race.py --session srv-9f3b --disconnect-after 5.2 --reconnect-after 6.1 --resume-token abc123 --idempotency acme-req-20260310-18-15
```

maria_cs: @priya_sre and @dan_engineer please own the postmortem and mitigation. Priya, can you confirm if we should extend the resume window or add a transient lock that prevents new requests being accepted while finalize is in-progress?

priya_sre: proposing quick patch: on resume_accept, set finalize_grace=15s and mark session immutable for new-request acceptance. That avoids double acceptance but needs careful memory accounting. I'll open an infra ticket with logs and suggested diff.

reconnect-bot: incident-update: credit_issued customer=acme amount=1_completion reason=duplicate_charge_pending_review :white_check_mark:

customer_acme: thanks all, appreciate the credit and the repro steps — let me know if you need additional traces from our side. :pray:
